title: Bind SCHC sender ACKs to authenticated peer, session, replay freshness, and final window
description: Security review finding in python/src/lichen/schc/fragment.py handle_ack_bytes: the sender accepts any canonical ACK carrying the same Rule ID. A C=1 ACK immediately marks the transfer successful without proving the ACK came from the intended authenticated peer/current fragmentation session, without replay-freshness enforcement, and without requiring the ACK window to identify the final window. A delayed valid ACK from an earlier transfer or another peer can therefore falsely complete a new transfer and discard retransmission state.
acceptance_criteria: ACK processing receives or is called only after verified local identity, remote signer identity, fragmentation Rule ID, and link replay-counter/session context are available. It binds those values to the active sender session, rejects unauthenticated or wrong-peer ACKs and replay counters not fresh for that session, and accepts C=1 only for the active transfer's final window. Tests cover a prior-session delayed C=1 ACK, an ACK from the wrong authenticated peer, a C=1 ACK for a non-final window, replayed ACK rejection, and successful completion by a fresh valid final-window ACK. Run three independent correctness, security, and robustness code-review passes and file every resulting finding before closure.
